programme_groups.title: UNCAP UN-NATO-AU 2025 technical-cooperation programme
programme_groups.interpretation: Retrospective confirms meetings and delegation visits, not a separate count per mention. April workshop has an independent dated source; May/June visits remain grouped. 2026-2028 package is prospective, not evidence of its delivery.

existing_mechanisms.title: LCM coordination and training marketplace
existing_mechanisms.implication: Use existing LCM systems and training schedule, with differentiated access and course ownership, rather than recommend a parallel portal.

existing_mechanisms.title: Deployment Review application
existing_mechanisms.implication: LCM/DPO, DOS and DGC already collaborate on review tooling. Test interoperability and reusable non-sensitive taxonomies instead of assuming a new tool is needed.

identity_tests.rule: Keep December and January-February cohorts separate; article total 22 is nonadditive.
Two publications do not establish two seminars.
Count one joint mission, not one per partner or language.
Do not create a field-activity count for each course component.
Shared administration is testable; qualifications and readiness outcomes cannot be substituted.
Related IT topics do not prove repeat attendees or duplicated teaching.
Related programme V5G001 is not another countable individual event.
13 represented Member States cannot be converted to 13 participants.

opportunities.title: Federated training administration using existing LCM infrastructure
opportunities.share: Course identifiers, provider/host roles, calendar updates and completion-status interfaces where access is authorized
opportunities.protect: DPO content authority; specialized certification; mission readiness; provider ownership; personal data
opportunities.baseline: LCM marketplace and training schedule already exist; expansion is not a new platform saving
opportunities.next_test: Map UNSOS IMTC course metadata to existing LCM and ITS fields; test access and interoperability before extending to DPPA providers

opportunities.title: One technical training-needs assessment per jointly scoped programme
opportunities.share: Agreed needs-assessment questions, capability descriptions, evidence references and controlled course-development assets
opportunities.protect: UN, AU and NATO approvals; mission-specific security; specialist instruction; 2026-2028 prospective outputs
opportunities.baseline: Joint assessment and planning are already observed, not newly invented consolidation
opportunities.next_test: Obtain published assessment/output inventories and identify genuinely identical input requests rather than merge partner deliverables

opportunities.title: Joint field-mission source packet with separate analytical approvals
opportunities.share: Approved itinerary, common non-sensitive chronology, evidence references and administrative arrangements
opportunities.protect: Political judgments; confidential contacts; ECOWAS/Commonwealth responsibilities; CNMC legal function; separate Council reports
opportunities.baseline: Sierra Leone mission is already joint; common source collection is not a second mission eliminated
opportunities.next_test: Trace explicit reuse of a source packet in separately mandated products; require shared-event identity, not geographical similarity

opportunities.title: Common training logistics across distinct UNSOS technical cohorts
opportunities.share: Permissible venue, scheduling, enrollment administration, translation and procurement templates
opportunities.protect: Aviation rescue, screening, liaison and IT curricula; separate cohorts; safety outcomes
opportunities.baseline: No duplicated venue booking, invoice or paid instructor service has been identified
opportunities.next_test: Match dates, locations, learning needs and eligible cost objects; do not assume multiple courses used substitutable purchases

opportunities.title: Reusable local supplier-orientation materials
opportunities.share: UN supplier-registration guidance, accessible templates and generic briefing materials
opportunities.protect: Separate solicitation specifications, competition, evaluation independence and vendor personal data
opportunities.baseline: One co-organized seminar is observed, not a double-paid procurement service
opportunities.next_test: Compare public materials across UN purchasing entities before proposing one common orientation module

opportunities.title: Reuse existing review-tool taxonomies instead of duplicate software
opportunities.share: Approved lessons categories, non-sensitive evaluation questions and export definitions where applicable
opportunities.protect: Restricted deployment reviews, staff confidentiality and distinct performance responsibilities
opportunities.baseline: Deployment Review application already jointly produced; supervisory course is only an adjacent workflow lead
opportunities.next_test: Verify authorized API/export capabilities and audience compatibility; no transfer of restricted records to this public repository
